text:
The Canadiens made the move of their season on Sunday, getting Dylan Larkin from Detroit for a package built around Kirby Dach and prospect Michael Hage, per NHL.com. It ended a saga that began with Larkin's trade request last summer and ran through a suspension in October. He centred Alex Newhook and Alexandre Texier in his debut Monday, and his forecheck set up Newhook's tying goal, per The Hockey News' Karine Hains. Montreal still lost 2-1 to the Kings.

The trade makes sense when you look under a 14-7-4 record. Montreal has 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our standings model has it about six points ahead of its play. The difference is rookie Jacob Fowler: the team has allowed about 12 fewer goals than its chances against predict, and Daily Faceoff calls him the easy Calder favourite, and maybe a Vezina candidate.

Lane Hutson is the other reason. His pair with Noah Dobson takes 58% of the expected goals, and the Montreal Gazette asked where the team would be without him. Phillip Danault's line with Texier and Zachary Bolduc has been the best forward group by chances (61%). But Juraj Slafkovský is running cold, with 3 points in 10 games against 7.6 expected, and Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks.

Our playoff odds have Montreal at 64%. What we'd watch: whether Larkin moves the 5-on-5 numbers enough that Fowler doesn't have to carry it.
headline: Larkin arrives for a team leaning on its rookie goalie
